title: Kyber’s Q3 2026 Update: Enterprise Features and Partnership Expansions
summary: Kyber’s Q3 2026 update highlights stronger enterprise capabilities, new carrier go-lives, deeper Guidewire connectivity, and continued progress into policy workflows.
body_markdown:
Q3 focused on strengthening the platform and enterprise controls behind Kyber’s claims correspondence workflows.


Building on Q2’s focus on review, governance, and the humans in the loop, the quarter centered on extending those capabilities across live carrier processes: helping more teams automate correspondence, strengthening connections with core systems and delivery channels,and building advanced administrative controls


### **Core Theme: Strengthening Enterprise Capabilities**


For carriers, faster drafting is only one part of managing correspondence. Teams also need control over access and dependable systems as correspondence moves through daily operations.


That’s why Q3’s infrastructure and administrative work matters. Engineering updates and custom roles addressed the platform behind the experience, while new go-lives showed Kyber in use in carrier workflows. Q3 focused on continuing to build a stronger operating foundation that can scale with the complexity and demands of enterprise-scale operations.


## **Major Product & Platform Updates**


## **HIPAA Compliance**


Kyber achieved HIPAA compliance in Q3, marking an important milestone in supporting larger enterprises with more complex security, privacy, and compliance requirements.


The milestone strengthens the security and compliance foundation behind Kyber as carriers automate more of the correspondence lifecycle. It also expands the range of workflows Kyber can support while maintaining the controls, governance, and data-handling standards required by enterprise insurance organizations.


## **Custom Roles**


[Custom Roles](http://www.askkyber.com/resources/custom-roles) became generally available this quarter, giving carriers more control over how different users access and interact with Kyber. Teams can define permissions around who can create, edit, review, approve, and manage correspondence based on role and responsibility.


## **Review Agents**


[Review Agents](http://www.askkyber.com/resources/review-agents) moved into broader beta availability across Kyber partners in Q3. Built on top of Kyber’s existing review processes, Review Agents are designed to pre-review correspondence and surface issues before documents reach a human reviewer.


## **Platform Infrastructure & Reliability**


Kyber’s new policy form builder is being designed to give carriers a central place to manage forms, endorsements, underwriting manuals, and related policy content, alongside tools for traceability, system syncing, and internal workflows.


## **Guidewire PolicyCenter Accelerator**


Kyber is also extending its Guidewire integration beyond ClaimCenter. We’re developing a new[PolicyCenter accelerator](https://marketplace.guidewire.com/product/kyber-accelerator-for-policy-correspondence-for-policycenter/01tKj00000Pw34xIAB?tab=Media) that will connect policy data and workflows with Kyber, supporting a more direct link between policy information and correspondence management.


## **Customer Growth & Adoption**


Q3 brought continued progress across carrier implementations, adoption, and expansion, with more examples of how carriers are putting governed correspondence automation into practice.


- [CFM Insurance and Forreston Mutual went live with Kyber through Ember](http://www.askkyber.com/news/ember-goes-live-with-kyber?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=internal&utm_campaign=2026_q3_update) , marking the first phase of a broader rollout across Ember’s mutual carrier partners.
- [Mutual of Enumclaw selected Kyber](http://www.askkyber.com/news/ember-goes-live-with-kyber?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=internal&utm_campaign=2026_q3_update) to modernize claims communications and support a more efficient, responsive experience for its members.
- [Openly highlighted how shifting template management ownership](http://www.askkyber.com/news/from-weeks-to-minutes-how-openly-put-template-management-back-in-the-hands-of-the-business-with-kyber?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=internal&utm_campaign=2026_q3_update) **** to business teams reduced IT bottlenecks and brought template updates down from weeks to minutes.
- [Aspire General highlighted how an early technology investment](http://www.askkyber.com/news/aspire-customer-story?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=internal&utm_campaign=2026_q3_update) in Kyber developed into a broader automation partnership, including automating more than 40% of its claims correspondence within one quarter.


Together, these examples show Kyber supporting carriers at different stages - from new implementations and expansion to measurable operational impact.


## **Partnerships & Ecosystem Expansion**


For correspondence automation to work in practice, it has to connect cleanly with the systems carriers already use. In Q3, Kyber continued building around that requirement through its work with Guidewire across[ClaimCenter](http://www.askkyber.com/news/kyber-launches-guidewire-accelerator-for-claims-correspondence-in-claimcenter?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=internal&utm_campaign=2026_q3_update) and[PolicyCenter](https://marketplace.guidewire.com/product/kyber-accelerator-for-policy-correspondence-for-policycenter/01tKj00000Pw34xIAB?tab=Media) . Kyber also published new joint content on turning claim data into clearer claimant communications, while continuing development around deeper core-system connectivity.


Together, these capabilities extend the correspondence workflow beyond document generation, connecting drafting and review with delivery and claim-file recordkeeping.


## **Market Engagement & Community**


Q3 created more opportunities to spend time directly with claims, technology, operations, product, and compliance leaders across the industry.


We hosted Friends of Kyber gatherings in Boston and Columbus, bringing together peers for informal conversations outside of the traditional conference environment.


The team was also on the ground at NAMIC’s 131st Annual Convention in Denver, and ITC Vegas 2026, which all created additional opportunities to hear directly from claims and technology leaders.


Across these conversations, several modernization priorities surfaced consistently: automating without sacrificing control, working effectively within existing core systems, driving adoption across claims organizations, and incorporating AI into day-to-day claims operations in practical ways.


## **Team & Culture**


Q3 brought new energy and continued growth across the Kyber team, with[Madison Cho](https://www.linkedin.com/in/madisoncho) joining marketing and[McKenzie Warren](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mackenzie-warren) as an Enterprise Account Executive.


Madison joined Kyber with experience helping build early-stage brands from the ground up, and is now leading work across content, community, events, and go-to-market storytelling. McKenzie brought a background in B2B SaaS and enterprise technology, with experience across regulated markets, and spent much of the quarter meeting carriers and industry peers across conferences and Friends of Kyber events.


Our first UX/UI design intern also wrapped up her time with us.[Sriharika](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sriharika-angadala/) ’s summer internship was celebrated with a rooftop BBQ and her final “culture report” on the team, a collection of her insights and unique learnings about each of the team members.


## **Looking Ahead to Q4**


Our focus in Q4 is centered on extending governed automation across more of the claims and policy workflow.


Key priorities include:


- **Review & Automation:** Expanding how correspondence can move from drafting through review, approval, delivery, and logging with less manual intervention.
- **Enterprise Controls & Compliance:** Strengthening permissions, governance, compliance, and administrative capabilities for larger organizations with more complex operating requirements.
- **Claude MCP:** Expanding how Kyber can connect with AI assistants and agentic workflows through Claude MCP, while keeping access to claims data and correspondence capabilities structured and governed.
- **Policy Workflows:** Launching the Guidewire PolicyCenter accelerator and beginning the rollout of Kyber’s policy form builder.
- **Ecosystem Expansion:** Deepening integrations with core systems, delivery providers, and technology partners to reduce handoffs between systems.
- **Implementation Scale:** Helping new carriers go live while supporting existing partners as they extend automation across more workflows.


## **Closing Perspective**


Q3 marked another step in Kyber’s evolution from AI-assisted drafting toward more connected, governed automation across claims operations.


Across the quarter, those shifts showed up in practice through broader carrier adoption, stronger integrations and delivery capabilities, more mature enterprise controls, and continued progress into policy working processes.


In Q4, the focus remains on extending that foundation: reducing more of the manual work surrounding correspondence while giving carriers the control, visibility, and structure required to operate at scale.
